caption: A medical worker pushes a patient in a wheelchair along a dark path after a hospital strike in Kyiv.

Qusra, West Bank A member of Israeli security forces aims his weapon at Palestinians during an attack by settlers in the West Bank village of Qusra. Israel’s president chose Gadi Eisenkot, Benjamin Netanyahu’s ⁠strongest rival, to ⁠try to ​form a new government. Eisenkot has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity, decrying recent incidents as ‘Jewish terror’ abetted by Netanyahu’s government.

Gaza A boy walks past flooded tents and wrecked cars after heavy rainfall in Gaza. Tens of thousands of Palestinians were left in waterlogged and damaged tents after deadly storms at the weekend, while 150,000 new shelters were being held outside Gaza awaiting Israeli approval to enter, aid agencies have said.

Gaza Palestinians walk through a camp housing displaced people amid buildings destroyed by Israeli strikes in Gaza City. NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, has been seen by more than 1.5 million people since being released in cinemas across the world last month.

Khan Younis, Gaza Staff inspect the damage inside Nasser hospital after an Israeli airstrike in Khan Younis. The strike killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.
Gaza A Palestinian bride prepares for a mass wedding celebration organised by Operation Chivalrous Knight, a humanitarian relief campaign, in Gaza.

Moscow, Russia Novaya Gazeta staff hold up portraits of slain journalists as they hold a last editorial meeting before the newspaper shuts down, citing what it described as a relentless campaign by the authorities, in Moscow. On 29 October, two things became known: Novaya was being evicted from its newsroom, and banks would stop processing readers’ donations to Novaya (its only legal income). Insiders spoke of the risk of Novaya being declared an extremist organisation – then any employee could be jailed: a journalist, an editor, an accountant or a cleaner.

Kraków, Poland A woman reacts at the site of a shooting near the main market square in Kraków. Six people were killed and 16 wounded after a gunman opened fire in the busy market square in what Poland’s defence minister called an ‘act of terror’ on the people of the city.

Madrid, Spain Protesters march during a general strike demanding wages that allow access to what demonstrators say is decent housing in Madrid. Millions of people across Spain joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power.
Paris, France Police officers clash with demonstrators at Place de la Nation during a protest over economic concerns organised by a coalition of student organisations and trade unions in Paris.

Paris, France A woman photographs rubbish bins blocking access to the Lycée Colbert in Paris. In recent weeks, youth-led protests have begun to sweep Europe , from school students in France demanding better conditions in which to work to those in Spain who pitched tents to rally for affordable housing.

New York City, US Rescuers search for victims in the rubble a day after a building collapsed in Brooklyn. Six people were ​found dead in the wreckage and two ‌others died later from their injuries, according to city ‌officials. Two of those killed were children and another two have been identified as construction workers from a nearby site.
Washington DC, US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed and his wife Sarah Jukaku ride the senate subway from the US Capitol to the Hart Senate office building.

Tehran, Iran An Iranian woman volunteer uses a zipwire at a military training centre for citizens at Azadi Square in Tehran. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said this week that it had targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.

Lima, Peru Pope Leo XIV and Peru’s president, Keiko Fujimori, watch a dancer performing at the Grand National Theatre of Peru in Lima. Tens of thousands lined the streets of Lima as Leo’s cavalcade drove him from the airport to the presidential palace when he arrived back in the country on Wednesday.
Manaquiri, Brazil A fisherman inspects dead fish along the shores of Lake Manaquiri, a tributary of the Amazon, in the rural area of Manaquiri.

Antalya, Turkey The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is greeted by an indigenous delegate at the Cop31 UN climate conference in Antalya. More than 100 corporations and industry groups linked to fossil fuel interests have sent delegations to the UN climate talks in Turkey , according to an analysis.
Dakar, Senegal A young girl rides a wave near the shore at Ngor beach in Dakar.

Tougaloo, Mississippi, US The Democratic senator-elect Scott Colom greets his family at the conclusion of a victory rally at Tougaloo College. Colom is the first black senator to be elected in Mississippi since the 1880s.
